x: Collaboration boundaries Pointer location describes transient activity. It belongs in awareness, while edits belong in the shared document or CRDT. Transports manages that state and connection lifecycle; Spaday binds it to page state. spaday-collab projects relative pointer coordinates and optionally displays them. Stable target IDs let a pointer refer to the same record when users have different viewport sizes, sort orders, or local selections. A component adapter translates those IDs into current geometry. Missing or obscured targets have no visible pointer. The package does not choose user identities, colors, roles, rooms, or tab grouping. Applications supply those policies. CodeMirror selections and decorations remain editor-specific; table and tree identity and geometry remain component-specific. A page can use scoped awareness without installing this package, or use its tracker with a custom display and transport. Removing a pointer component disconnects its observers and listeners. Blur, page hiding, and leaving a target withdraw local pointer state. Network disconnects, reconnects, and stale-peer expiry remain the awareness connection’s responsibility. These boundaries allo

Run python -m spaday_collab.example and leave Share my pointer across the page checked. The checkbox controls local sharing; remote pointers remain visible when it is unchecked. The example’s js/examples/page-pointers.js wraps a PointerAdapter: pointers.adapter = pageTargets(componentAdapter, true); A component target takes priority. Otherwise, the wrapper uses a normalized viewport position. Target IDs are prefixed to distinguish component targets from the page fallback. This helper is example code, not a package export; copy it into your application and wrap the same adapter used for table rows, tree items, or ordinary HTML. Viewport positions show approximate activity when users have different page layouts or scroll positions. Component positions identify the same content. If a component target is missing or off-screen in the receiving browser, its pointer stays hidden; the example does not reinterpret it as a page position. Blur, leaving the page, and awareness disconnects still withdraw pointers.

Run the local example in two browsers. Focus the shared note as Alice: Bob sees “Alice: Focused” beside it. Type to show “Alice: Editing”; after 1.5 seconds without input, the label returns to “Focused”. Press Tab to move the focus indicator to the review section. Moving the pointer does not change keyboard focus. To adapt this behavior, copy js/examples/focus.js and the awareness mapping in js/examples/example.js. The helper reports {target, editing, selection?} or null, using the focused HTML element’s nearest data-collab-target. Keep this state alongside the pointer in one awareness value so updating either field preserves the other. Use SetField("pointer", event_value("pointer")) for pointer events, then compose the awareness value in the store subscription as the example does. Render each remote target’s labels through ordinary Python components and textContent bindings. Clear focus on window blur, hidden pages, and navigation. Disconnect the helper when removing the page integration. The managed awareness connection removes disconnected peers and republishes current local state after reconnect. Select text in Alice’s shared note to show a colored highlight in Bob’s textarea. Collapse the selection to show a caret; a backward selection places that caret at its active end. Each browser uses its own wrapping, textarea size, and scroll position. The overlay ignores pointer input. The example helper js/examples/text-selection.js measures text in a hidden mirror of the textarea and draws the remote ranges above it. Focus changes publish the textarea’s UTF-16 anchor and head offsets along with the exact text snapshot. Only matching snapshots render, so a model update arriving before its awareness update hides stale marks. Empty text and trailing newlines still have caret positions. Blur, target changes, and disconnected peers remove the marks. This small-note example includes the note text in awareness to validate offsets. It does not transform selections through concurrent edits or turn the textarea into a text CRDT. Use spaday-codemirror’s anchored selections for collaborative code editing; keep this mirror and snapshot policy in example code.

Use Share my activity in the local example to control each outgoing signal independently: Control Default Remote display Page-text selections On Selected text highlighted in matching content. Focus and textarea selections On Focus/editing labels and textarea ranges/carets. Click indicators Off A colored marker that fades after 800 ms. Viewport position Off A percentage showing approximate progress down the page. Turning a control off withdraws that local state. It does not hide incoming activity. The pointer checkbox remains independent. All signals use the same awareness connection. For ordinary text, mark static, non-overlapping blocks with unique data-collab-text IDs. The js/examples/page-selection.js helper splits a native selection across those blocks and sends exact text snapshots plus UTF-16 offsets. The receiver resolves its own text nodes, rejects mismatched snapshots, and uses the CSS Custom Highlight API to paint ranges without replacing its local selection. Keep form controls, private text, and presence labels outside these opted-in blocks. Browsers without that API omit the page highlights. js/examples/page-activity.js demonstrates click and viewport sharing. Clicks us

Import connectPointers from /components/collab/cdn/index.js. Pass a geometry adapter, a callback for local state, and a callback for projected remote coordinates. Call render(remotePeers) when awareness changes and disconnect() when removing the integration. No Pointers element is required.

Set --spa-collab-accent, --spa-collab-label-text, or --spa-collab-z-index on the page or component. A peer’s explicit color overrides the default accent. Use spaday-pointers::part(cursor), ::part(label), and ::part(hover) for additional styling. Mount the overlay outside transformed or clipped containers so fixed positioning uses the page viewport.

SpadayPointers.adapter accepts a PointerAdapter. The default is domTargets(document), which selects [data-collab-target] elements. Target IDs must be unique within that adapter. Multiple overlays can use disjoint roots. PointerAdapter has: hitTest(x, y): string | null: target ID under viewport coordinates. resolve(id): Geometry | undefined: current target geometry. roots?(): (Element | ShadowRoot)[]: observed mutation, resize, and scroll roots. Defaults to the document body. Geometry has bounds: DOMRectReadOnly, optional visibleBounds: DOMRectReadOnly, and hit(x, y): boolean. Bounds and hit tests use viewport coordinates. elementGeometry(element) returns DOM bounds, ancestor clipping, and a hit test. domTargets(root = document) creates an adapter for ordinary HTML targets beneath that root; shadow-root contents require their own adapter root. connectPointers(adapter, changed, draw) returns: current(): last local pointer or null. render(peers): project {peer, pointer} entries through current geometry. refresh(): recheck local geometry and schedule remote drawing. disconnect(): remove listeners and observers, withdraw the local pointer, and clear the display. Run shared pointers Install the example dependencies: pip install "spaday-collab[examples]" python -m spaday_collab.example Open http://127.0.0.1:8044/ in one browser and http://127.0.0.1:8044/bob in another. Move Alice’s pointer over the note. Bob’s browser shows an orange arrow and label over the same part of the note. Resize Bob’s window and move Alice’s pointer again. The pointer remains relative to the note, even when each window has a different layout. Edit the note in either browser. Both display the updated text through the same transports connection that exchanges pointer awareness. Move outside the targets or close one browser; its pointer disappears from the other. See the example source for the Python page and the awareness mapping for the application adapter.

from spaday import SetField, element, event_value from spaday_collab import Pointers page = element( "main", element("section", "Review this section", **{"data-collab-target": "review"}), Pointers() .bind("peers", "remote_pointers") .on("pointer-change", SetField("local_pointer", event_value("pointer"))), ) A pointer is {target, x, y} with coordinates between zero and one. Remote entries are {peer, pointer, label?, color?}. The application maps scoped awareness into this list and chooses labels and colors. The included example uses Spaday’s Wire.awareness and one transports connection for both shared data and pointers. The browser module also exports connectPointers, domTargets, and elementGeometry. These work without the Pointers renderer or a transports connection.

pip install "spaday-collab[examples]" python -m spaday_collab.example Open http://127.0.0.1:8044/ and http://127.0.0.1:8044/bob in separate browsers. The Share my pointer across the page checkbox enables a viewport fallback outside the note and review section. Over those targets, pointers follow the same content in the other browser. Focus the note or Tab to the review section to show a focus label in the other browser. Typing briefly changes that label to “Editing” while the shared note updates. Select text to show a remote highlight, or place the caret to show its position. Share my activity also controls page-text highlighting, transient click markers, and optional viewport progress; receiving activity never scrolls or activates controls. Demo identities are selected by URL; production applications must authenticate users and assign permissions on the server.
